demographics.trauma_type: Accidentally caused serious injury to another

Triggers.value: Weapons or objects used as weapons

Memory.value: When I remember the event I feel overwhelming grief
There are parts of the event that I simply cannot remember no matter how hard I try
Sometimes I feel the full emotional intensity of the event without any clear image or memory

vignette: Maria, a 43-year-old widowed Latin American woman working as a cybersecurity analyst, has been struggling with a profound sense of guilt and grief since an incident at work that occurred six months ago. As a cybersecurity analyst, Maria often deals with complex systems and high-stakes security threats. On the day of the traumatic event, she was demonstrating a new cybersecurity tool to her colleagues when a malfunction led to a critical system failure. Unbeknownst to Maria, this failure caused an injury to one of her coworkers who was trying to intervene. Since then, Maria has been haunted by triggers that remind her of this incident. Her workplace now holds numerous reminders—weapons-like objects like heavy tools used for repairs or any confrontation with colleagues. Whenever she encounters these triggers, vivid memories flood back. For instance, a colleague’s attempt at discussing the incident can set off intense feelings of grief and sorrow, as if the event were happening all over again. The memory gaps are particularly distressing; she cannot recall crucial details of how the malfunction occurred or exactly what happened in those critical moments. Maria has found that these memories often arise without any clear image, just a powerful wave of emotion. She feels intense guilt and anguish, yet lacks a coherent visual memory to contextualize her feelings. This leaves her feeling helpless and anxious, as she cannot make sense of the fragmented pieces of the event that keep resurfacing. The grief associated with these memories is overwhelming. The more she tries to avoid thinking about it, the more potent the triggers become. Even mundane objects can set off a chain reaction—her eyes might catch sight of a tool used for repairs, and suddenly she’s back in that moment, re-experiencing the intense emotions without any clear visual memory. Maria has been isolating herself from her colleagues to avoid these confrontations and triggers. Her work environment, which was once a source of pride, now feels like a minefield of potential reminders. She often leaves meetings early or avoids them altogether, leading to strained relationships with her coworkers and a noticeable decline in her professional engagement. Despite her efforts to maintain a semblance of normalcy, Maria’s emotional state has deteriorated. The memories continue to haunt her, especially during moments when she is alone. What frightens her most is the fear that she will never be able to fully understand or process what happened. Her sense of self-worth has been deeply affected; she constantly questions whether she can ever trust herself again. Maria’s decision to seek help came after a particularly distressing encounter with a colleague who inadvertently triggered a severe memory recall, leaving her in tears and unable to function at work for days afterward. She is most hoping that therapy will provide her with the tools to navigate these memories and triggers without feeling overwhelmed by guilt and grief. Her ultimate goal is to regain some sense of control over her life and return to the level of professional engagement she once enjoyed. Through it all, Maria has been holding on to a glimmer of hope—that with support, she can find a way to heal and rebuild her life.
